readings.title: Jacob's Last Request
readings.subtitle: Jacob's Final Oath
readings.text: [Genesis 47:28] And Ya’aqoḇ lived in the land of Mitsrayim seventeen years. So the days of Ya’aqoḇ, the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years. [29] And the days of Yisra’el drew near to die, and he called his son Yoseph and said to him, “Now if I have found favour in your eyes, please put your hand under my thigh, and show kindness and truth to me. Please do not bury me in Mitsrayim, [30] but let me lie with my fathers, and you shall take me out of Mitsrayim and bury me in their burial place.” And he said, “I do as you have said.” [31] And he said, “Swear to me.” And he swore to him. And Yisra’el bowed himself on the head of the bed.

readings.title: Jacob Blesses Yoseph's Sons
readings.subtitle: The Blessing of Ephraim and Manasseh
readings.text: [Genesis 48:1] And it came to be after these events that it was said to Yoseph, “See, your father is sick.” And he took with him <dn>את</dn> his two sons, <dn>את</dn> Menashsheh and <dn>את</dn> Ephrayim. [2] And Ya’aqoḇ was told, and said, “See, your son Yoseph is coming to you.” And Yisra’el strengthened himself and sat up on the bed. [3] And Ya’aqoḇ said to Yoseph, “<dn>Ěl Shaddai</dn> appeared to me at Luz in the land of Kena’an and blessed me, [4] and said to me, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am making you fruitful and shall increase you, and shall make of you a community of peoples, and give <dn>את</dn> this land to your seed after you as an everlasting possession.’</dq> [5] And now, your two sons, Ephrayim and Menashsheh, who were born to you in the land of Mitsrayim before I came to you in Mitsrayim, are mine – as Re’uḇĕn and Shim’on, they are mine. [6] And your offspring whom you bring forth after them are yours, and are called by the name of their brothers in their inheritance. [7] And as for me, when I came from Paddan, Raḥĕl died by me in the land of Kena’an on the way, when there was but a little distance to go to Ephrath. And I buried her there on the way to Ephrath, that is Bĕyth Leḥem.” [8] And Yisra’el saw <dn>את</dn> Yoseph’s sons, and said, “Who are these?” [9] And Yoseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom <dn>Elohim</dn> has given me in this place.” And he said, “Please bring them to me, and let me bless them.” [10] And the eyes of Yisra’el were dim with age, he was unable to see. And he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them. [11] And Yisra’el said to Yoseph, “I had not thought to see your face, but see, <dn>Elohim</dn> has also shown <dn>את</dn> me <dn>את</dn> your seed!” [12] So Yoseph brought them from between his knees, and he bowed down with his face to the earth. [13] And Yoseph took <dn>את</dn> them both, <dn>את</dn> Ephrayim with his right hand toward Yisra’el’s left hand, and <dn>את</dn> Menashsheh with his left hand toward Yisra’el’s right hand, and brought them near to him. [14] And Yisra’el stretched out <dn>את</dn> his right hand and laid it on Ephrayim’s head, who was the younger, and <dn>את</dn> his left hand on Menashsheh’s head, consciously directing <dn>את</dn> his hands, for Menashsheh was the first-born. [15] And he blessed <dn>את</dn> Yoseph, and said, “The <dn>Elohim</dn>, before whom my fathers Aḇraham and Yitsḥaq walked, the <dn>Elohim</dn> who has fed <dn>את</dn> me all my life long to this day, [16] the <dn>Messenger</dn> who has redeemed <dn>את</dn> me from all evil, bless <dn>את</dn> the youths! And let my name be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Aḇraham and Yitsḥaq. And let them increase to a multitude in the midst of the earth.” [17] And Yoseph saw that his father laid <dn>את</dn> his right hand on the head of Ephrayim, and it was evil in his eyes. So he took hold of his father’s hand to remove <dn>את</dn> it from Ephrayim’s head to Menashsheh’s head. [18] And Yoseph said to his father, “Not so, my father, for this one is the first-born. Lay your right hand on his head.” [19] But his father refused and said, “I know, my son, I know. He also becomes a people, and he also is great. And yet, his younger brother is greater than he, and his seed shall become a completing of the nations.” [20] And he blessed them on that day, saying, “By you Yisra’el shall bless, saying, ‘<dn>Elohim</dn> make you as Ephrayim and as Menashsheh!’ ” Thus he put <dn>את</dn> Ephrayim before Menashsheh. [21] And Yisra’el said to Yoseph, “See, I am dying, but <dn>Elohim</dn> shall be with you and bring <dn>את</dn> you back to the land of your fathers. [22] And I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.”

readings.title: Jacob's Prophecy to His Sons
readings.subtitle: The Twelve Tribes
readings.text: [Genesis 49:1] And Ya’aqoḇ called his sons and said, “Gather together, so that I inform you <dn>את</dn> what is to befall you in the last days: [2] Gather together and hear, you sons of Ya’aqoḇ, and listen to Yisra’el your father. [3] Re’uḇĕn, you are my first-born, my power and the beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity and the excellency of power. [4] Boiling over as water, you do not excel, because you went up to your father’s bed, then you defiled it – he went up to my couch. [5] Shim’on and Lĕwi are brothers, weapons of violence are their swords. [6] Let my being not enter their council, let my esteem not be united to their assembly; for in their displeasure they slew a man, and in their self-will they lamed an ox. [7] Cursed be their displeasure, for it is fierce, and their wrath, for it is cruel! I divide them in Ya’aqoḇ and scatter them in Yisra’el. [8] Yehuḏah, you are the one your brothers praise. Your hand is on the neck of your enemies, your father’s sons bow down before you. [9] Yehuḏah is a lion’s whelp; from the prey, my son, you have gone up. He bowed down, he lay down as a lion. And as a lion, who shall rouse him? [10] The sceptre shall not depart from Yehuḏah, nor an enactor of Law from between his feet, until Shiloh comes, and to Him is the obedience of peoples. [11] Binding his donkey to the vine, and his donkey’s colt to the choice vine, he washed his garments in wine, and his robes in the blood of grapes. [12] His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk. [13] Zeḇulun dwells by the haven of the sea, and he is for a haven of ships, and his border is toward Tsiḏon. [14] Yissaḵar is a strong donkey, lying down between two burdens. [15] And he saw that rest was good, and <dn>את</dn> the land that it was pleasant, and he inclined his shoulder to bear a burden, and became a subject to slave labour. [16] Dan rules his people as one of the tribes of Yisra’el. [17] Dan is a serpent by the way, a horned snake by the path, that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider falls backward. [18] I have waited for Your deliverance, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! [19] Gaḏ, a raiding band raids him, but he raids at the last. [20] From Ashĕr, his bread is fat, and he yields royal dainties. [21] Naphtali is a hind let loose, he gives pleasant words. [22] Yoseph is a fruit-bearing bough, a fruit-bearing bough by a fountain, his branches run over the wall. [23] And the archers have bitterly grieved him, and shot at him and hated him. [24] But his bow remained in strength, and the arms of his hands were made strong by the hands of the <dn>Mighty One of Ya’aqoḇ</dn> – from there is the <dn>Shepherd</dn>, the <dn>Stone of Yisra’el</dn>, [25] from the <dn>Ěl</dn> of your father who helps you, and by the <dn>Almighty</dn> who blesses you with blessings of the heavens above, blessings of the deep that lies beneath, blessings of the breasts and of the womb. [26] The blessings of your father have excelled the blessings of my ancestors, up to the utmost bound of the everlasting hills. Let them be on the head of Yoseph, and on the crown of the head of him who was separated from his brothers. [27] Benyamin is a wolf that tears, in the morning he eats prey, and at night he divides the spoil.” [28] All these are the twelve tribes of Yisra’el, and this is what their father spoke to them. And he blessed <dn>את</dn> them, he blessed each one according to his own blessing.

readings.title: The Death and Burial of Jacob
readings.subtitle: Jacob's Death and Burial
readings.text: [Genesis 49:29] And he commanded <dn>את</dn> them and said to them, “I am to be gathered to my people. Bury <dn>את</dn> me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite, [30] in the cave that is in the field of Maḵpĕlah, which is before Mamrĕ in the land of Kena’an, which Aḇraham bought <dn>את</dn> with the field of Ephron the Hittite as a possession for a burial place. [31] There they buried <dn>את</dn> Aḇraham and <dn>את</dn> Sarah his wife, there they buried <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq and <dn>את</dn> Riḇqah his wife, and there I buried <dn>את</dn> Lĕ’ah – [32] the purchase of the field and of the cave that is in it was from the sons of Ḥĕth.” [33] And when Ya’aqoḇ had ended commanding <dn>את</dn> his sons, he drew his feet up into the bed and breathed his last, and was gathered to his people. [Genesis 50:1] And Yoseph fell on his father’s face and wept over him, and kissed him. [2] And Yoseph commanded <dn>את</dn> his servants <dn>את</dn> the physicians to embalm <dn>את</dn> his father. So the physicians embalmed <dn>את</dn> Yisra’el. [3] And forty days were completed for him, for so are completed the days of embalming. And the Mitsrites wept for him seventy days. [4] And when the days of his weeping were past, Yoseph spoke to the household of Par'oh, saying, “If, now, I have found favour in your eyes, please speak in the ears of Par'oh, saying, [5] ‘My father made me swear, saying, “See, I am dying. In my burial place which I dug for myself in the land of Kena’an, there you bury <dn>את</dn> me.” And now, please let me go up and bury <dn>את</dn> my father, and return.’ ” [6] And Par'oh said, “Go up and bury <dn>את</dn> your father, as he made you swear.” [7] And Yoseph went up to bury <dn>את</dn> his father. And with him went up all the servants of Par'oh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Mitsrayim, [8] and all the house of Yoseph, and his brothers, and his father’s house. Only <dn>את</dn> their little ones, and <dn>את</dn> their flocks, and <dn>את</dn> their herds they left in the land of Goshen. [9] And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen, and it was a very great company. [10] And they came to the threshing-floor of Ataḏ, which is beyond the Yardĕn, and they lamented there with a great and very severe lamentation. And he observed seven days of mourning for his father. [11] And when the inhabitants of the land, the Kena’anites, saw the mourning at the threshing-floor of Ataḏ, they said, “This is a severe mourning for the Mitsrites.” Therefore its name was called Aḇĕl Mitsrayim, which is beyond the Yardĕn. [12] And his sons did to him as he had commanded them. [13] For his sons carried <dn>את</dn> him to the land of Kena’an, and buried <dn>את</dn> him in the cave of the field of Maḵpĕlah, before Mamrĕ, which Aḇraham bought <dn>את</dn> with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a possession for a burial place.

readings.title: Joseph Reassures His Brothers
readings.subtitle: Joseph's Mercy to His Brothers
readings.text: [Genesis 50:14] And after he had buried <dn>את</dn> his father, Yoseph returned to Mitsrayim, he and his brothers and all who went up with him to bury <dn>את</dn> his father. [15] And when Yoseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “What if Yoseph hates us, and pays us back for <dn>את</dn> all the evil which we did to <dn>את</dn> him?” [16] So they sent word to Yoseph, saying, “Before your father died he commanded, saying, [17] ‘This is what you are to say to Yoseph, “I beg you, please forgive the transgression of your brothers and their sin, for they did evil to you.” ’ And now, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your father.” And Yoseph wept when they spoke to him. [18] And his brothers also went and fell down before his face, and they said, “See, we are your servants.” [19] And Yoseph said to them, “Do not fear, for am I in the place of <dn>Elohim</dn>? [20] And you, you intended evil against me, but <dn>Elohim</dn> intended it for good, in order to do it as it is this day, to keep a great many people alive. [21] And now, do not fear, I provide for <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> your little ones.” And he comforted <dn>את</dn> them and spoke to their hearts.

readings.title: The Death of Joseph
readings.subtitle: Joseph's Oath and Death
readings.text: [Genesis 50:22] And Yoseph dwelt in Mitsrayim, he and his father’s house. And Yoseph lived one hundred and ten years. [23] And Yoseph saw Ephrayim’s children to the third generation. The children of Maḵir, son of Menashsheh, were also born on Yoseph’s knees. [24] And Yoseph said to his brothers, “I am dying, but <dn>Elohim</dn> shall certainly visit <dn>את</dn> you, and bring <dn>את</dn> you out of this land to the land of which <dn>He</dn> swore to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya’aqoḇ.” [25] And Yoseph made <dn>את</dn> the sons of Yisra’el swear, saying, “<dn>Elohim</dn> shall certainly visit <dn>את</dn> you, and you shall carry up <dn>את</dn> my bones from here.” [26] And Yoseph died, being one hundred and ten years old. And they embalmed <dn>את</dn> him, and he was placed in a coffin in Mitsrayim.
